title: Analytic framework for the lift of F : N(L) -> C(L) into Stokes data
scope: Phase IV restricts the analytic lift to scalar linear ODEs at an irregular singularity x = infinity. Difference (Birkhoff-Trjitzinsky) and q-difference (Ramis) Stokes phenomena have analogous structures but require separate frameworks; they are documented but not analysed here.
Levelt_Turrittin: For a meromorphic connection at x = infinity with one irregular singularity and Katz invariant p/q in lowest terms, after pulling back to the ramified cover x = t^q the formal connection splits as a direct sum of rank-one summands whose irregular types are polynomials Q_i(t) in C[t] of degree <= p. The leading coefficient c_i of Q_i is the i-th root of the WKB characteristic polynomial chi(c) from Phase I.
irregular_type: On the cover t-plane, each formal solution carries a factor exp(Q_i(t)) times a formal monodromy factor t^{nu_i}. The collection (Q_i, nu_i) is the *irregular type* and forms the discrete part of the wild character variety.
anti_Stokes_directions: For an ordered pair (i, j) of formal exponentials, the anti-Stokes direction is the set of arguments phi of t at which Re(Q_i(t) - Q_j(t)) = 0 to leading order. Writing Q_i - Q_j = L_{ij} t^{d_{ij}} + lower order, where L_{ij} is the leading coefficient and d_{ij} = deg(Q_i - Q_j) <= p, the anti-Stokes directions in the t-plane satisfy arg(L_{ij}) + d_{ij} * phi = pi/2 (mod pi), yielding 2 d_{ij} directions in [0, 2 pi). In the generic case d_{ij} = p and L_{ij} = c_i - c_j = Delta_{ij}; in degenerate cases d_{ij} < p (leading terms cancel).
Stokes_sectors: The complement of the union of anti-Stokes directions in the t-plane is a disjoint union of open sectors. On each sector S, there is a unique multi-summation lifting the formal solution to a holomorphic one, and the dominance order Re(Q_i(t)) > Re(Q_j(t)) is constant on S.
Stokes_groups: Stokes multipliers between adjacent sectors form unipotent matrices whose support (nonzero off-diagonal entries) is constrained by the dominance order across the shared anti-Stokes direction: entry (i, j) is allowed only when Q_j dominates Q_i on the *positive* side of the direction. The Stokes group at a given anti-Stokes direction is the unipotent subgroup of GL_N(C) generated by all such allowed entries.
wild_character_variety: The wild character variety MW(L) parametrises {formal monodromy} x {Stokes data} / {gauge}. As an algebraic variety its dimension equals the irregularity of L; its discrete strata are indexed by (i) the multiset of leading coefficients {c_i} (= the constellation C(L)) and (ii) finer invariants of the irregular type (lower-order Q_i coefficients, formal monodromy).
difference_q_difference_remark: For difference operators, Stokes phenomena occur in vertical strips and are organised by the Birkhoff connection coefficients; for q-difference operators, Ramis's theta-Stokes structure replaces sectors with annular regions. The constellation C(L) and Delta_{ij} data continue to make sense in both contexts (they are combinatorial), but the anti-Stokes-direction picture does NOT translate verbatim. We document this gap and treat scalar ODEs only in the lifting.
key_references_for_notation: Wasow / Sibuya (asymptotic existence and Stokes phenomenon)
Iwasaki, Kimura, Shimomura, Yoshida (Painleve Stokes graphs)
